title: CRJA/30/2013 of Karanveer AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Criminal Jail Appeal No.30 of 2013

Karanveer & Anr. Ö..ÖAppellants
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ..ÖÖ.Respondent
Mr. Prashant Khanna, Amicus Curiae for the appellants
Mr. Sandeep Tandon, Deputy Advocate General along with Mr. Lalit Miglani, Brief
Holder for the State
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.

This criminal jail appeal is directed against the
judgment and order dated 19.06.2013 passed by Sessions
Judge, Chamoli in Sessions Trial No.15 of 2012 State vs.
Karanveer & Anr., whereby the appellants have been
convicted under Section 363 of IPC and have been
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period
of three years along with fine of ` 1,000/- each. In default
of payment of fine, the appellants have been directed to
undergo three monthsí additional imprisonment.
2. Prosecution story, in brief, is that on
12.07.2012 P.W.3 (complainant) lodged a report at P.S.
Karnprayag District Chamoli stating that his daughter is
student of class IX and her date of birth is 17.02.1998. On
11.07.2012 she had gone to her school but did not come
back. He tried to search her but to no avail. He was
informed that her daughter was seen with two boys in bus
station. Then he could know that the appellants have
enticed away his daughter. On the basis of report, a case
was registered under Section 363 and 366-A of IPC against
the appellants. Investigation of the case was handed over
to PW7 Sub Inspector Rakesh Kumar Saini, who during
the course of investigation, recorded the statement of

2
witnesses and prepared the site-plan of the place of
incident. On 13.07.2012, the prosecutrix was recovered
from the custody of the appellants, a fard whereof was
prepared by the I.O.; appellants were arrested and
thereafter the statement of the prosecutrix were recorded
before the Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. On
completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed against
the accused/appellants for their trial under Sections 363
and 366-A of IPC. After hearing the parties, charge was
framed against the accused/appellants under the
aforesaid sections. The charge was read over and
explained to them, to which they pleaded not guilty and
claimed to be tried. On this, prosecution got examined
PW1 complainant and father of the prosecutrix, PW2
prosecutrix, PW3 Jaswant Singh Negi, PW4 Vinod Kunwar,
PW5 Lakhpat Singh Rawat, PW6 Constable Ganesh Bhatt
and PW7 Sub Inspector Rakesh Kumar Saini, Investigating
Officer of the case. Thereafter, the statements of the
accused/appellants were recorded under Section 313 of
Cr.P.C. in the form of questions and answers. In reply,
they stated that they are innocent and they have been
falsely implicated in the case. However, they did not any
lead any evidence in defence. The trial court, after hearing
the prosecution and defence, found the
accused/appellants guilty of offence punishable under
Section 363 of IPC and sentenced them accordingly.
However, the accused/appellants were acquitted of the
charge of offence punishable under Section 366-A of IPC.
3. PW1 complainant is the father of the
prosecutrix. He reiterated the averments made in the FIR
lodged by him. He has supported the case of the
prosecution.

3
4. PW2 prosecutrix stated that on the date of
incident she was studying in Class IX. Her date of birth is
17.02.1998. She stated that she came in contact with the
appellant on phone. On 11.07.2012 she went to school
with her father. After school hours, the appellants met her
at the school gate. Before that on the last night, the
appellants had called her on mobile and that told her that
they will come to take her from school. At 01:00 PM,
appellant came to her school and took her to Karnaprayag
by Tata Sumo. On that day, they stayed at Karnaprayag
waiting room. She tried to contact her father but the
appellants told her that they will tell her father. On
12.07.2012, appellants took her to Gauchar. Thereafter
she was taken to Badrinath but as the road was blocked
they could not reached there. On 13.07.2012 they
returned to Gauchar and at about 09.30 am, police
apprehended them. Thereafter, she was medically
examined at Gopeshwar Hospital and her statements were
recorded u/s 164 of Cr.P.C.
5. PW3 Jaswant Singh Negi has stated that he is
Principal of the Vidhya Niketan, Gairsain since 2008. The
prosecutrix was student of Class IX and as per school
record her date of birth is 17.02.1998.
6. PW4 Vinod Kunwar has stated that on
11.07.2012 he had seen the prosecutrix sitting in Tata
Sumo after school hours. When he came to know that the
prosecutrix has not returned from school, he disclosed
this fact to her father.
7. PW5 Lakhpat Singh Rawat, Gram Pachayat
Development Officer has proved the date of birth of the
prosecution as 17.02.1998.

4
8. PW6 Constable Ganesh Singh is a formal
witness. He has proved the written report Ext.A1 and chik
FIR Ext.A8 as well as G.D. entry Ext.A9.
9. PW7 Sub Inspector Ramesh Kumar Saini,
Investigating Officer, has stated that on 12.07.2012 he
was posted as Sub Inspector at P.S. Karnaprayag. He was
entrusted with the investigation of the case. During the
course of investigation, he recorded the statements of
witnesses, prepared the site-plan and recovered the girl
from the custody of the appellants. Prosecutrix and the
appellants were brought to the police station whereafter
the prosecutrix was sent for medical examination. On
26.07.2012 statement of the prosecutrix was recorded u/s
164 of Cr.P.C. and on concluding the investigation, he filed
the charge-sheet against the appellants under Section 363
and 366-A of IPC.
10. As stated earlier, there is no challenge to the
findings recorded by the trial court in respect of acquittal
of the accused/appellants under Section 366-A of IPC.
Thus, the findings of the trial court, acquitting the
appellants for the offence punishable under Section 366-A
has become final.
11. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the entire record.
12. Learned Amicus Curiae would submit that as
per own statement of the prosecutrix, both the appellants
met her on the school gate and asked her to accompany
her and she accompanied them on such requested made
by them. He would submit that it is a clear case of consent
between the prosecutrix and the appellants and in such

5
circumstances, the conviction of the appellants under
Section 363 of IPC is illegal and the appellants deserve to
be acquitted. In the alternative, learned Amicus Curiae
would submit that the sentence awarded to the appellants
is excessive. He would submit that the appellants were
aged about 19 and 22 years respectively on the date of
incident and were not mature enough to know the
consequences and implications of their act. It is also
submitted that out of the total sentence awarded the
appellants have served out more than fourteen months of
incarceration and hence a prayer has been made for
reduction in sentence.
13. Contrary to this, learned Deputy Advocate
General would submit that the prosecutrix was minor on
the date of incident, hence, consent is irrelevant in the
present case.
14. There is no dispute with regard to the fact that
the victim was a minor on the date of incident. Sufficient
evidence, disclosing the age of victim, were produced
before the trial court, on the basis of which the trial court
arrived to the conclusion that the victim was a minor on
the date of incident. The evidence regarding the age of
victim has been well discussed and evaluated by the trial
court.
15. Now, the sole question which falls for
consideration of this Court is as to whether on 11.07.2012
the accused/appellants kidnapped the prosecutrix, a
minor girl, from lawful guardianship of her parents.

6
16. As observed earlier, the prosecutrix was a minor
on the date of occurrence. In her statement, she has
stated that the appellants met her on the school gate and
asked her to sit in the Tata Sumo. She has specifically
stated that she tried to contact her parents while staying
in Karnaprayag but the appellants did not allow her to do
so. Although she has not stated anywhere that she was
forced to sit or that she was under threat but the fact
remains that the appellants carried her to Karnapayag and
Gauchar out of the lawful guardianship. Thus, from the
record, it is clearly established that the prosecutrix was
enticed away by the appellants. That being the position,
the offence punishable under Section 363 IPC is clearly
made out against the appellants wherefor they have been
rightly convicted.
17. Having given my anxious consideration to the
evidence on record, I do not see any reason to differ with
the findings recorded by the trial court regarding
conviction of the appellants under Section 363 of IPC.
However, on the point of sentence, I find some force in the
arguments advanced by learned Amicus Curiae. The Trial
Court has sentenced the appellants to undergo rigorous
imprisonment for a period of three years along with a fine
of ` 1,000/- each under the aforesaid Section. At this
juncture, Section 363 of IPC would be apt to mention,
which is reproduced hereunder:-
363. Punishment for kidnapping.óWhoever kidnaps
any person from 1[India] or from lawful
guardianship, shall be punished with imprisonment
of either description for a term which may extend to
seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

7
18. A perusal of the aforesaid Section makes it clear
that there is no minimum punishment prescribed under
Section 363 of IPC. That being so, as also in view of the
fact that the appellants have served out more than
fourteen months of sentence out of the total sentence
awarded, I am of the considered view that ends of justice
would be met, if the punishment awarded to the
appellants is reduced to the period already undergone by
them.
19. Accordingly, criminal appeal is partly allowed
while upholding the conviction of the appellants. However,
for the reasons stated above, sentence of imprisonment is
modified to the extent that the appellants are sentenced to
the period of sentence already undergone by them.
Sentence of fine, awarded by the trial court, shall remain
intact.
20. Appellants are on bail. They need not surrender.
Their bail bonds are cancelled and sureties are discharged.
21. Let a copy of the judgment be immediately sent
to the trial court for ensuring compliance. Lower court
record be also sent back.
